cards.question: A family flees gang violence but stays within Haiti’s borders. Which term best describes them?
cards.answerExplanation: The border is the key distinction. Internally displaced people have been forced from home but remain inside their own country; refugees have crossed an international border.
cards.whyNow: Global Voices reported that Haiti’s continuing security crisis is forcing more people from their homes and into relocation.

newsPegSources.headline: Haiti’s security crisis forces displacement and relocation

cards.question: A tanker passing through the Strait of Hormuz travels between Iran and which country’s Musandam Peninsula?
cards.answerExplanation: The strait’s northern shore is Iran, while Oman’s Musandam Peninsula forms the opposite side. That narrow geography helps explain the route’s outsized importance to energy shipping.
cards.whyNow: A White House release put control of the Strait of Hormuz back into the news today; the EIA reference independently establishes the geography.

coreFactSources.title: The Strait of Hormuz is the world’s most important oil transit chokepoint

newsPegSources.headline: President Trump Was Right: America Controls the Strait of Hormuz

cards.question: Heavy rain continues upstream, but downstream gauges suddenly show the river falling. Which development best explains the drop and warns of a later surge?
choices: A debris dam is blocking the river and storing water upstream
A tributary flood crest is adding water just below the gauges
Rapid snowmelt is increasing inflow near the river’s source
A reservoir release is sending a pulse down the main channel
cards.canonicalAnswer: A debris dam is blocking the river and storing water upstream
cards.answerExplanation: A debris blockage can cut downstream flow while water pools behind it. If the temporary dam overtops or breaches, the stored water can arrive downstream as a sudden surge.
cards.whyNow: The Guardian reported that rescue operations are continuing after deadly floods in Nepal and Tibet, bringing Himalayan flood hazards back into focus.

coreFactSources.title: Assessment of existing and potential landslide hazards resulting from the April 25, 2015 Gorkha, Nepal earthquake sequence

newsPegSources.headline: Number of missing in Nepal and Tibet rises to nearly 3,000 as operations continue

cards.question: If a lunar spacecraft on a free-return trajectory cannot make another major engine burn, what can still bend its path back toward Earth?
cards.answerExplanation: A free-return trajectory is shaped so the Moon’s gravity redirects the spacecraft onto an Earth-returning path. It does not depend on another major propulsion maneuver.
cards.whyNow: NASA honored the Artemis II crew after its completed lunar flyby, bringing the mission’s free-return flight design back into the news.

coreFactSources.title: Final Steps Underway for NASA’s First Crewed Artemis Moon Mission

newsPegSources.headline: NASA’s Artemis II Crew Receives Congressional Space Medal of Honor

cards.question: An abandoned metal mine keeps acidifying a stream even after operations stop. What can keep producing the acid?
choices: Sulfur-bearing rock exposed to air and water
Carbonate rock sealed away from groundwater
Quartz grains buried beneath impermeable clay
Native copper stored in dry, oxygen-free rock
cards.canonicalAnswer: Sulfur-bearing rock exposed to air and water
cards.answerExplanation: Many mine rocks contain sulfide minerals. When they contact oxygen and water, oxidation can form sulfuric acid and leach metals, so polluted drainage can continue long after a mine closes.
cards.whyNow: Global Voices reported continuing health and water impacts from copper and cobalt mining pollution in Lualaba, Democratic Republic of Congo.

newsPegSources.headline: The devastating impact of copper and cobalt mining pollution in Lualaba, DRC
